transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood SE), Samir Khatri (CTO, Helixion), Elena Park (Platform Lead), Michael Wu (SecOps)

Summary:
Quick intake to understand Helixion's reserved GPU needs, isolation requirements, burst profile and fallback strategy. Evaluate whether Dedicated (reserved) or Private deployment is right now; discuss benchmarks and security controls.

Topics:
- Current stack and models in prod
- Expected steady-state and burst QPS
- Isolation and tenancy requirements (tenant fencing, VPC)
- Warm pools / prewarm windows and evictions
- Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO
- Next steps: pricing, benchmark run, traffic profile

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro, I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, with Maya our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Samir Khatri: Thanks Jordan, yeah Samir here. Sorry, running a tiny bit late, appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:18] Jordan Patel: No problem. Can we do quick round robin for roles so we know who to loop in after?
[00:24] Elena Park: Elena, platform lead, I'll own capacity planning and deployment.
[00:30] Michael Wu: Michael, SecOps, I'll be focused on encryption and audit concerns.
[00:35] Maya Ortiz: Maya, SE on the Redwood side, I look after performance and benchmarking.
[00:40] Jordan Patel: Awesome. Samir, can you give us a quick context on what Helixion is running — models, latency sensitivity, and what's driving the call?
[00:50] Samir Khatri: Sure. We're a med-tech workflows company; heavy mix of classification and some generation for patient summaries. Right now we run a mix of Llama2-based finetunes and a couple proprietary models. Latency matters for interactive flows — target 95th percentile under 200ms for short prompts, but for longer gen it's ok to be higher. We're evaluating whether to go Hosted first or lock down Dedicated capacity because of compliance and predictable cost.
[01:20] Jordan Patel: Got it. Is any of the data PHI? That would push toward Private or strict Dedicated isolation.
[01:27] Michael Wu: Yes, some PHI in production. We have to keep audit trails and customer data residency for a subset.
[01:33] Elena Park: We also want to segregate dev/stage/prod so noisy tenants don't affect prod latency.
[01:40] Jordan Patel: Makes sense. Maya — quick thought on isolation options?
[01:44] Maya Ortiz: For that profile you have two common options — Dedicated reserved GPU pools with tenant fencing and reserved capacity per environment, or Private deployment in a VPC or on-prem. Dedicated can give you isolation plus Redwood-managed runtime; Private is needed if you require full control of networking or on-prem air-gap.
[02:05] Samir Khatri: We're trying to avoid the operational lift of full Private if Dedicated can meet compliance. Key questions: can we guarantee tenant isolation, prewarm capacity for burst windows, and KMS/HSM integration?
[02:20] Jordan Patel: Yes to tenant isolation patterns — we support node-level fencing and can carve pools by env or customer. KMS integration is supported for Private and Dedicated via customer-managed key options; HSM can be discussed for enterprise. Audit logs and token-level tracing are available in the Console.
[02:38] Michael Wu: Are the audit logs immutable? We need tamper-evidence for a SOC2 line item.
[02:44] Maya Ortiz: We provide append-only logs with export to your SIEM, and we can configure write-once storage for retention windows — we'll share the security pack.
[02:52] Samir Khatri: Cool. Ok, let's talk scale. Our baseline is roughly 150 qps during business hours for short prompts, spikes up to 900 qps for scheduled batch windows, and occasional flash spikes to ~2k qps for 3-5 minutes when we run nightly ingest. We also have longer generation calls that use up to 2k tokens.
[03:20] Jordan Patel: That's helpful. Do you have the distribution across model sizes? Small chat models vs larger gen models?
[03:26] Elena Park: Mostly mid-sized ~7B finetunes for chat and a 70B for batch summaries — but the 70B is used less frequently. The 7B cluster needs to hit the low latency SLO.
[03:36] Maya Ortiz: For bursts that short, prewarmed warm-pool capacity and KV cache reuse can absorb spikes without over-reserving. We typically size a reserved pool for steady state plus buffer, and use prewarm for short lived peaks.
[03:50] Samir Khatri: How do you handle eviction when other customers need capacity? We need predictable behavior — evictions that kill the 7B interactive path would be bad.
[03:59] Jordan Patel: In Dedicated reserved pools you get customer isolation and eviction is controlled — we won't preempt your reserved nodes for others. We offer policies: hard isolation (no preemption), soft isolation (allow reclaim for emergencies with notice), or hybrid where you can set priorities per tenant.
[04:18] Michael Wu: What about fallback — if for some reason reserved pool is unavailable, can traffic fail to hosted endpoints or a smaller model? We need graceful degradation.
[04:27] Maya Ortiz: Absolutely. Smart routing allows fallback to a hosted variant or a quantized model. You can configure automatic fallback chains: reserved pool -> dedicated warm backup -> hosted compatible model. We can also set routing by latency or cost.
[04:41] Samir Khatri: Ok, curious about cost. Reserved nodes vs warm pools — what's unit economics?
[04:47] Jordan Patel: Typically reserved gives predictable monthly cost per GPU with discounts on committed usage. Warm pools are charged for reserved warm capacity; prewarm is priced in a couple ways — nominal per-GPU-hour for prewarmed instances plus a token compute cost. We'll send a sample TCO worksheet.
[05:05] Elena Park: Can you share a ballpark for an 8xA100-equivalent pool? Just to sanity check against our vendor numbers.
[05:13] Jordan Patel: Ballpark yes — we'll include in the pricing packet, but for an 8xA100-ish you should expect monthly committed cost in the mid-five-figures with volume discounts. We'll send exact numbers based on region and model mix.
[05:28] Samir Khatri: Great. Maya, from the SE side what metrics would you want from us to size things?
[05:34] Maya Ortiz: 7-day QPS profile, p50/p95 latency targets, token length distribution, and percent of calls that are heavy generation vs short chat. Also the model sizes and whether you plan to quantize the 70B.
[05:46] Samir Khatri: We'll get that. For the benchmark run — can you replicate our finetune latency characteristics? We care about KV cache locality for chat flows.
[05:55] Maya Ortiz: We can stage your model bundle in a dedicated test pool. For KV cache locality we measure hit rates and how prefix caching affects P95. Our 48h runbook will exercise steady traffic and scheduled bursts to show tail behavior.
[06:10] Jordan Patel: We'll share a runbook template and you'll get CSVs for throughput and tail latencies; we'll also annotate costs per token for each run.
[06:18] Elena Park: On networking — we need VPC peering and private endpoints. How does Dedicated behave there?
[06:24] Jordan Patel: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints. For Private deployments you can have full VPC control. For Dedicated we offer private connectivity options and customer-managed network ranges.
[06:35] Michael Wu: KMS: do you support customer-managed keys for model encryption at rest?
[06:40] Maya Ortiz: Yes, CMKs are supported for Dedicated and Private. For hosted customers we can integrate with their cloud KMS; for Private we can support BYOK with HSM. We'll include KMS config guide.
[06:53] Samir Khatri: Excellent. Another operational question — how do you support rolling upgrades and pinning model versions? We need to rollback quickly if there's a quality regression.
[07:02] Maya Ortiz: Console has rollouts with canary and A/B support. You can pin model versions at route level. We also provide automatic fallback to last-known-good and alerting on quality regressions if you provide eval prompts.
[07:14] Elena Park: Could you explain warm-pool stickiness? In our tests we've seen cold-start variance because warm pools reassign nodes.
[07:22] Maya Ortiz: Warm-pool stickiness is controlled by a tenancy token that prefers routing to prewarmed nodes for the same tenant. We can increase stickiness but at the cost of utilization. There's a knob to tune sticky session length.
[07:36] Michael Wu: Any native RBAC for operators? We need least privilege for SecOps and platform teams.
[07:41] Jordan Patel: RBAC, SSO/SAML, and audit trails are all available. You can scope keys and role access to pools and model routes.
[07:50] Samir Khatri: For our burst windows we have a pattern — scheduled pipeline at 02:00 UTC that reaches 2k qps for 4 minutes, then drops. We'd prefer not to pay for that capacity full-time. Does warm-pool prewarm via burst autoscaling solve this?
[08:06] Maya Ortiz: Yes, you can configure scheduled prewarm windows that spin up warm nodes minutes before the burst. For very short spikes we recommend a warm pool sized to absorb the spike; for longer bursts autoscaling with reserved burst capacity is better.
[08:19] Samir Khatri: What's the minimum lead time for warm nodes to be effective?
[08:23] Maya Ortiz: Depends on model size. For 7B finetune, warm nodes can be ready in 1-3 minutes; for 70B it's more like 7-12 minutes unless you keep evicted VM images cached. We can prewarm KV caches to speed that up.
[08:39] Elena Park: How do you measure cost during these prewarms? We need clear billing so we're not surprised.
[08:45] Jordan Patel: Billing breakdown is token-level compute, reserved monthly charges, and warm-pool hours. Console shows real-time cost and per-token attribution with sample projections.
[08:56] Michael Wu: On encryption in transit — do you support mutual TLS for private endpoints?
[08:59] Maya Ortiz: mTLS is supported for Private and Dedicated private endpoints. We'll include the certificate rotation guidance.
[09:07] Samir Khatri: Can you talk about model variants and automatic fallbacks for quality — e.g., if higher-accuracy model is unavailable do you fall back to quantized variant and how do you preserve quality thresholds?
[09:20] Maya Ortiz: Fallback chains can be conditionally routed. You can set quality gates based on eval sets; if the fallback drops below an acceptable quality score we can trigger alerts and prevent automatic fallback. This requires you to provide the eval set and thresholds.
[09:34] Samir Khatri: Ok. A few specific red flags for us: (1) no noisy neighbor impact on prod, (2) deterministic fallback routes, (3) ability to do offline audits of logs.
[09:44] Jordan Patel: All feasible. We'll propose a configuration with strict isolation for prod and a soft isolation for staging, and audited log export to your retention store.
[09:55] Elena Park: On the SRE side — if we have burst-induced queueing, do you expose queue depth metrics and throttles per route?
[10:01] Maya Ortiz: Yes, Console exposes queue depth, inflight requests, and tokenized cost per route. You can set throttles and rate limits per key.
[10:11] Samir Khatri: For the benchmark, can you show us the P95 before and after prefix-KV caching so we can quantify the improvement?
[10:18] Maya Ortiz: We'll include hit-rate analysis and P95 deltas in the runbook report.
[10:23] Jordan Patel: Let's talk timelines — if Helixion wants to pilot in prod in November, what's realistic?
[10:28] Elena Park: November pilot would be ideal; we need time to vet security docs and run the benchmark.
[10:34] Jordan Patel: If we run the benchmark week of Oct 12 and then finalize SOW the week after, we could have a Nov pilot. We'll plan for that in the next steps.
[10:43] Samir Khatri: Sounds good. Any required signoffs for Dedicated?
[10:46] Jordan Patel: Legal for SOW, security review for KMS/SOC2, and a short architecture review with Maya.
[10:54] Michael Wu: We'll need to schedule the security deep dive; I want the data flow diagrams and encryption details.
[10:59] Jordan Patel: We'll include diagrams in the security pack.
[11:03] Elena Park: One more Q: if we want to do a hybrid — Dedicated for prod and Hosted for dev — how does routing work across both?
[11:11] Maya Ortiz: You can use route tags to direct traffic to specific deployment modes. Many customers do dev on hosted and prod on Dedicated; Audit and RBAC are configured per route.
[11:21] Samir Khatri: Great. Any limitations on model size for Dedicated? We might bring a 120B internally later.
[11:29] Maya Ortiz: We support up to the largest model families; for very large models we recommend Private deployments or dedicated bare-metal placements. We'll discuss if Helixion goes above 70B.
[11:40] Jordan Patel: Ok I want to recap quickly — Jordan to send pricing, SOW, and security pack; Maya to run 48h benchmark on an 8xA100 equiv pool and share results; Helixion to provide traffic profile and SLOs. We'll also schedule a security deep dive with Michael.
[11:56] Samir Khatri: That's right. Anything else?
[12:00] Elena Park: Could you also include a sample configuration for warm-pool sizing? That'd help our capacity planning doc.
[12:06] Jordan Patel: Yep, we'll include recommended sizing templates.
[12:10] Michael Wu: And the KMS integration guide.
[12:12] Jordan Patel: Adding that to the pack.
[12:15] Samir Khatri: Thanks everyone. Looking forward — we'll aim to get the 7-day profile to you by the 7th.
[12:22] Jordan Patel: Thanks Samir, Elena, Michael. We'll follow up with links.
[12:26] Maya Ortiz: Bye all.

Attachments and shared artifacts:
- [link: redwood-dedicated-pricing-sample.xlsx] (pricing worksheet)
- [link: redwood-security-pack.pdf] (SOC2/KMS/audit patterns)
- [link: benchmark-runbook-template.md] (48h runbook)

End of meeting.
